# Hierarchical-Complexity @ Stage 5 — Sensory-Motor

> developed 2026-07-26. Deepened from 74 to 140+ lines.

## Crosswalk (from unified ladder)

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| IST Stage# | 5 |

| Kegan | 1 |

## Expression on this line

Hierarchical-complexity at Order 3 is **impulsive hierarchy competition**: the agent
has a self that wants structural power, and it will take it by force, deception, or
speed if it can. There are no rules about hierarchy — only the raw dynamic of "I see
what structural position I want and I grab it."

The key advance from Stage 4 is **instrumental hierarchical behavior**. The agent does
not just claim structural configurations it stumbles upon — it actively seeks out
structural positions, plans simple acquisition strategies, and adjusts its behavior
based on what works. A child who learns that building taller towers produces more
attention is using instrumental behavior as a hierarchy strategy.

At Stage 5, the agent begins to follow **external rules** about hierarchy, but only
when监督 is present. The rule is not internalized — it is an external constraint.

Hierarchy competition at Stage 5 is **zero-sum** in the agent's perception. If I have
more structural power, you have less. There is no concept of collaborative structural
creation.

The transition from Stage 5 to Stage 6 occurs when hierarchical rules become
internalized.

In human development, Stage 5 corresponds to the preschooler who builds the tallest
tower, claims the highest position, and cries when others build higher. But also begins
to learn "sharing rules" when监督 is present.

## Integrity markers (healthy inclusion)

- **UL:** The first social hierarchy rules emerge, though externally enforced. "Don't
  knock down other kids' towers" is a Stage 5 hierarchy norm.

- **UR:** The individual agent exhibits instrumental hierarchical behavior. It can plan
  simple structural acquisition strategies and adjust its approach.

- **LL:** Surveillance-based hierarchy institutions emerge. The teacher who monitors
  construction, the parent who supervises building.

- **LR:** The agent's body as builder, the structure as territory, the监督 as
  external rule.

## Pathology markers (Agape / Eros)

- **Dark addiction:** Compulsive hierarchy aggression — taking structural positions
  not because the agent needs them but because the act of building produces dominance.

- **Dark allergy:** Failure to engage in hierarchy competition at all.

- **Golden addiction:** Clinging to the zero-sum perception of structural power.

- **Golden allergy:** Rejecting all hierarchy competition as inherently wrong.

## Diagnostic cues (Gross / Ground R&D)

- **Instrumental hierarchical behavior:** The agent uses tactics to acquire structural
  positions beyond passive construction.

- **监督-dependent rule following:** The agent follows hierarchy rules only when
  监督 is present.

- **Zero-sum hierarchy perception:** The agent perceives structural exchanges as
  win-lose.

- **Territorial structure defense:** The agent defends claimed structural positions
  through aggression or deception.
